Probleem in één zin Veel organisaties ve: Problem in one sentence Many organizations lose control as soon as AI agents and modern analytics tools need real-time access to business-critical data: data is fragmented, there is a risk of cloud or platform lock-in, and teams do not know who should make which decision when external conditions change. This prevents external signals (legislation, supplier disruption, market shifts) from being directly translated into business strategy, cash flows, processes and measures.
Kernbewijs (bron) Zetaris beschrijft een: Core evidence (source) Zetaris describes a federated cloud architecture that gives AI agents a secure, real-time route to enterprise data without lock‑in to a single cloud or platform (PR Newswire: “Zetaris Launches Cloud-Based AI Data Harness…”). Use this as technical evidence for the general problem: organizations need a secure, flexible layer to reliably connect AI to distributed data.
Waarom dit een ondernemingsprobleem is (: Why this is a business problem (plain language) - Strategy & objectives: External changes must filter into strategic priorities within weeks (not months). If data and decision information are not immediately available and reliable, decision-making slows and you lose first-mover advantage. - Money & investment: Unknown impact on revenue, margin and cash flow arises when external risks are not quickly quantified. The result: wrong prioritization of investments or delayed cost savings. - Processes & execution: Operations must be able to automatically convert signals into controlled process changes and escalations — otherwise incidents and manual fixes pile up. - People & roles: Without clear decision owners and defined actions, ‘who does what’ ambiguity arises; decisions remain unmade. - Risk & governance: Data access for AI must be controlled and auditable to manage compliance, privacy and security risks.
De praktische, herhaalbare lus (sluitend: The practical, repeatable loop (closed improvement cycle) For entrepreneurs and managers the distinguishing factor is that you implement and keep the following closed loop operational: 1) Signal (what do you observe?) — external or internal trigger: legislative text, shrinking supplier capacity, price shift, news about cyber incidents, internal inventory variance. 2) Context (what does it mean for your company?) — scope: which business units, products, revenue streams and processes are relevant? What is the uncertainty/timing? 3) Consequence (what could happen?) — concrete impact on strategy, costs, service levels and people; identify worst-, base- and best-case. 4) Decision (which choice is made?) — one explicit decision, with horizon and acceptable risks. 5) Action (who does what, when?) — owner (function/role), specific tasks, required resources and deadline. 6) Outcome (how do we measure success?) — one verifiable KPI or measurement point per action. 7) Learning (feedback to strategy/rules) — update decision rules, playbooks and priorities based on measured outcome.
Praktisch besluit‑template (direct toepa: Practical decision template (directly applicable) - Signal: New guideline X for data retention (external). - Context: Affects product group Y and customer contracts with retention period Z. - Consequence: Compliance risk + possible contract penalties; impact on IT costs due to need for additional storage management. - Decision: Establish a temporary retention-policy exception and start a technical migration to a federated data architecture for selected sources. - Owner (action): Chief Information Officer (CIO) — responsible for technical migration; Legal — responsible for policy exception and compliance check. - Action: 1) Legal publishes temporary retention-policy route within 7 working days; 2) IT builds connector for federated access to the three most critical data sources and activates logging/audit. - Measurement point (verifiable result): Number of critically linked data sources with auditable access = N (target: 	63 within 30 days) and percentage of compliance checks performed on migrated data = 100%. - Learning: After 30 days: evaluate whether the federated connection improved auditability and update the standard retention rules; record lessons learned in the decision register.
Waarom een federated data‑laag helpt (za: Why a federated data layer helps (business benefit) A controlled, federated data layer (the "data harness" the source refers to) makes it possible to: - Forward real-time signals to analytics and AI processes without moving data or creating vendor lock-in. - Centralize access and audit so compliance and security are preserved. - Base prioritization of actions on business-relevant metrics (strategy-to-operation linkage) instead of on raw data availability. POWERHOUSE is the engine in this picture that orchestrates the loop: it collects signals, provides context, monitors decision rules, organizes tasks and records outcomes and learnings — it is the process and decision layer, not the 'product' that a customer must purchase.
Checklist voor implementatie (minimum vi: Checklist for implementation (minimum viable governance) - Verify signal sources: news feeds, compliance alerts, vendor status, internal KPIs. - Define context templates per signal type (regulation, vendor, market) so scope analysis reports can be generated quickly. - Assign one decision owner per decision category (CIO, CFO, COO, Head of Sales, Legal). - Link each decision to a single metric (e.g. #datasources, %actions completed, time from decision to execution). - Use a simple, traceable audit log for data access and decision execution. - Write every lesson back into the decision register and update prioritization models.
